hints: Focus on what each definition strictly demands, formation needs 1 mole of product from elements only, combustion needs 1 mole of fuel burned in oxygen.
Check reaction 1 first, 1 mole of C(s) burns to make 1 mole of CO2(g) from its elements C and O2.
Now test the others for the strict rules, does reaction 2 make 1 mole and does reaction 3 start only from elements?
walkthrough:
**Recall the two definitions**

Remember the key conditions side by side. Formation is about the product.

$$\Delta H_f^\ominus: \text{1 mol of compound formed from its elements in standard states}$$

$$\Delta H_c^\ominus: \text{1 mol of a substance completely burned in oxygen}$$

**Test reaction 1**

Look at $\text{C(s) + O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$. One mole of carbon burns, so it is combustion of carbon.

At the same time, one mole of $\text{CO}_2$ is formed from its elements C(s) and $\text{O}_2$(g) in their standard states, so it is also formation of $\text{CO}_2$. Reaction 1 qualifies for both.

**Test reaction 2 and reaction 3**

Check $\text{2C(s) + O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{2CO(g)}$. Although elements make CO, it makes 2 moles, not 1 mole. The $\Delta H^\ominus$ for this equation is twice the standard molar value, so it fails the 1 mole rule.

Check $\text{CO(g) + }\frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$. One mole of CO burns, so it is combustion of CO. But CO is a compound, not an element, so it cannot be formation of $\text{CO}_2$. It fails the elements only rule.

**Conclude**

Only reaction 1 satisfies both definitions at the same time. So the correct choice is 1 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests 1, 2 and 3 all qualify. Reaction 2 fails because it involves 2 moles, and reaction 3 fails because CO is not an element.
options.B: Incorrect. This suggests 1 and 2 both qualify. Reaction 2 as written is $\text{2C + O}_2 \rightarrow \text{2CO}$, so its enthalpy is for 2 moles of CO and 2 moles of C, not the standard 1 mole value.
options.C: Incorrect. This suggests 1 and 3 both qualify. Reaction 3 is combustion of CO, but formation of $\text{CO}_2$ must start from elements C(s) and $\text{O}_2$(g), not from the compound CO(g).
options.D: Correct. Only reaction 1 qualifies. It burns 1 mole of C(s) and also forms 1 mole of $\text{CO}_2$(g) from its elements in standard states, so it is both $\Delta H_c^\ominus$ of carbon and $\Delta H_f^\ominus$ of carbon dioxide.
